## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Issariyakāmakārikādikathā* (Kv 23.3) is a debate located in the twenty-third chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. As observed by S. N. Dube, the compound title is unique in Pali literature, and the debate centers around the proposition *Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātam gacchati ti?*—examining whether a Bodhisatta enters an unhappy state or realm of ruin (*vinipāta*) deliberately through the exercise of sovereign choice or free will (*issariyakāmakārikā*), reflecting developments in the early Bodhisatta ideal [Dube 1980].

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse (285 matching segments across 27 texts) [DharmaNexus]. The largest matches involve stock doctrinal formulas shared with the *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44), *Vacchagotta Saṁyutta* (SN 33), *Cūḷamālukya Sutta* (MN 63), *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta* (DN 9), *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares passages with other debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, such as the *Niyāmokkantikathā* (Kv 4.8) and *Duggatikathā* (Kv 12.9), and is cited in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring automated alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Prajñāpradīpaṭīkā* (D3859) [DharmaNexus].
